key_insight: RetroChessBench exposes persistent failures in frontier-model reasoning when reconstructing legal chess histories and distinguishing possible events from forced ones.
engineering_relevance: Rule-governed reasoning systems need checks for legal constructions and exhaustive conclusions, even when code execution is available.
method: Introduce 12 retrograde-chess tasks covering exact-length constructions, unique endings, and exhaustive answer sets.
Provide references, scoring rubrics, and a terminal-reward environment.
Evaluate GPT 6 Astra High with and without code execution, using two trials per task per condition.
evidence_signal: Required final answers were not produced in 22/24 attempts without tools and 18/24 with code execution; mean terminal rewards were 14.75% and 27.19%, respectively.
watch_item: The evaluation is small and model-specific; limited exposure to worked retrograde explanations is a hypothesis, not an established cause of failure.
paper_title: RetroChessBench: A Benchmark for Reconstructing and Proving Chess Histories
